subject: Re: Trial acceptance metrics & ownership lanes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial acceptance metrics & ownership lanes

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. I wanted to capture the outcome and the agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth while your team reviews timelines. High-level recap below.

Goal for the 4-week trial: validate that Redwood can meet Novacorp’s latency and cost targets while producing acceptable QA for customer-facing summarization workflows.

Agreed acceptance metrics (first-pass, to be confirmed by your team):
- Latency: P95 endpoint response <= 400ms for 512-token average inference (50k tokens/day workload).
- Throughput: sustained 1200 requests/hour with no queueing above 300ms for the first token.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0018 (targeting quantized model + batching).
- Quality: ROUGE-L baseline >= 0.72 vs your internal gold set (we’ll run 200 sample prompts).

Owners / responsibilities:
- Novacorp: provide 200 labeled sample prompts & expected outputs by EOD Thu (Priya). Provide procurement checklist (Samir).
- Redwood: provide trial environment, run the 200-sample evaluation, and share token-cost breakdown + latency dashboard (Marissa / Ben).
- Ops gating: Rishi will own the smoke validation and post-deploy runbook.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight metrics template (novacorp-poc-metrics-template.xlsx) and the updated mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.pdf). Please flag edits directly in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEFghIJkLmno

Next steps (near-term):
1) Novacorp shares samples & procurement window by Thursday.
2) Redwood sets up a sandbox cluster and provides access + basic runbook within 48 hours of samples.
3) Joint kickoff to run the 200-sample evaluation and agree on the measurement script.

If that matches your notes, reply-all with any changes and we’ll lock the dates.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Trial acceptance metrics & ownership lanes

Marissa —

Thanks for the thoughtful recap — that aligns well. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with product & procurement:

- Samples: Priya will circulate the 200-sample set by Thursday EOD. These are redacted customer transcripts + internal expected summaries (we’ll mark the gold standard).
- Latency caveat: the 400ms P95 is acceptable for single-node tests but our production traffic includes some 99th percentile spikes we want to understand; can Redwood include a 99th percentile snapshot after the first week?
- Procurement: we have a procurement window that opens 7/28 and closes 8/11. If the trial demonstrates the targets, we’ll accelerate to a pilot procurement during that window.

One ask: can you surface an estimated cost delta between running the trial on Hosted vs Dedicated for our expected throughput? Budget will drive the procurement path.

Priya (cc) — once you share samples, Samir asked that you include a short note of which endpoints/flows are highest priority.

Samir
Director, AI Platforms | Novacorp
samir.patel@novacorp.com
Phone: +1 (212) 555-4444

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial acceptance metrics & ownership lanes

Marissa — copying technical next steps we should execute once samples arrive.

Tech plan (Ben):
1) Sandbox provisioning: we’ll provision a 2-GPU sandbox (A100 equivalent) with a pre-configured inference image and monitoring hooks. Target spin-up: 24h after samples + M-ACL.
2) Evaluation harness: I’ll drop a measurement script into the shared Drive that computes latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), throughput curves, and token accounting per call. It will also compute ROUGE-L and a basic semantic-similarity score.
3) Batching/quantization knobs: default run will use int8 quant and dynamic batching at 64ms latency cap; we’ll do a follow-up run with more aggressive batching if cost needs to be reduced.

Operational items for Rishi:
- Smoke tests: basic end-to-end runbook + canary script (we want a daily healthcheck).
- Alerting: set thresholds for p95>500ms and error rate >0.5% to notify both teams.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — quick status update and refined timeline now that we have commitments from both sides.

Confirmed intake: Priya shared the 200-sample set this morning (received). I pulled the files into the Drive and validated the expected-output column.

Updated timeline:
- 7/21: sandbox provisioned by Redwood (Ben) — access + runbook shared.
- 7/22-7/23: initial 200-sample run for baseline metrics.
- 7/24: joint review session (30m) to review ROUGE baseline and latency/throughput dashboards.
- 7/28 — 8/11: procurement window (Novacorp) — if gating thresholds are met we’ll hand over pilot pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ben: drop measurement script in Drive + run initial pass (7/22).
- Rishi: create smoke checklist and alert thresholds (7/22).
- Priya: confirm top-3 production flows for post-trial stress test (7/22).
- Samir: confirm procurement decision criteria for the pilot path (7/24).

One immediate ask for Samir — can you confirm whether we should include a 99th percentile latency target in the acceptance gates or keep it as an informational metric for the first demo? If you’d prefer it as a gate we’ll include a 99th <= 850ms condition on the final acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff tomorrow.

Best,
